subject: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted API vs current provider — post-call recap
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ahmed Khan <ahmed@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted API vs current provider — post-call recap

Hi Ahmed / Priya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps to qualify p95/p99 end-to-end latency for your production traffic: 

Summary of FinLytics requirements (as discussed)
- Primary targets: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency for inference requests (includes client network, edge, Redwood endpoint, model execution).
- Example targets (your initial numbers): p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 650ms for short completions (~<64 tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state ~50 requests/sec, with bursts to 200 rps; typical concurrency per model pool ~400 concurrent inferences.
- Streaming: need initial token to start arriving within 150-250ms for streaming endpoints; per-token arrival steady-state throughput target ~25-50 tokens/sec after stream start.
- SLA/observability: per-request token/latency breakdowns, sampling of full traces, and per-route cost/latency dashboards.

What we need from you to run a realistic comparison test
1) A recent 1–2 hour trace or sampled request log (timestamps, request/response sizes, token counts, client-region). Prefer OpenTelemetry traces but CSV logs are fine.
2) Typical payload sizes and batching behavior (do you send many short prompts or fewer long prompts).
3) Any hard constraints for initial token latency vs stream tail (e.g., UI requires first token < 200ms).
4) A short maintenance window (1–2 hours) for a controlled perf run, or a traffic mirror we can ingest safely.

Proposed Redwood deliverables
- Side-by-side p95/p99 comparison (hosted Redwood API vs your current provider) using your traces or a replay harness.
- Breakdown by network/edge/runtime/model (so you can see where tail latency originates).
- Suggested tuning: batching, caching, quantization, routing policy, and streaming knobs.
- PoC plan: 1) ingest traces, 2) run replay tests with identical request distribution, 3) 48-hour sanity run on your sample workload, 4) recap + recommendations.

Next steps
- If you can share traces, we can schedule a replay test next week (suggest Wed or Thu).
- We'll prepare a short perf matrix (attached) showing expected p95/p99 ranges across typical model sizes and quantization options.

Attachments: Redwood latency matrix (high-level): redwood-latency-matrix-2028-04.pdf

Thanks —
Jonas

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted API vs current provider — post-call recap

Jonas — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Our current SLA targets are: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 900ms (measured end-to-end). We see heavy tail during peak (>300 rps).
- Typical requests are 80% short prompts (~<100 tokens), 20% long. Average response token count ~45.
- Streaming is critical for our chat UI: we need first token within 200–250ms and continuous per-token updates at ~30 tokens/sec.

I've uploaded a sample traces bundle and a small CSV (request_id, ts_request, ts_response, token_count, region) to the Drive link you provided. Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/finlytics-traces-0408

We can support a replay window next Thursday (Apr 17) between 02:00–05:00 PDT. We'll coordinate with infra for a mirrored traffic stream.

One ask: we're sensitive about attaching raw traces with IPs — can Redwood sign a short NDA/POA for trace handling? Also, SOC 2 evidence requests will come up later in procurement.

Attaching: finlytics-currentprovider-traces.zip

—Ahmed

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted API vs current provider — post-call recap

Thanks Ahmed — this is perfect and very helpful. Quick replies inline + concrete next steps: 

- NDA/trace handling: yes — we can sign a short Trace Handling Addendum. I'll route to legal and share a DocuSign link by EOD today.
- Replay window: Thu Apr 17 02:00–05:00 PDT works. We'll run both Redwood hosted API and a replay against your recorded provider traces so the comparison uses identical input.
- Metrics and pass/fail criteria: propose we evaluate against the following measurable SLOs (end-to-end):
  * Short completions (<64 tokens): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms
  * Medium (64–256 tokens): p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms
  * Streaming initial token latency: <=200ms  (target)
  * Sustained token rate for streaming: >= 25 tokens/sec
  * No single model pool should exceed 2x baseline tail latencies under burst conditions; we will capture concurrency breakdowns.

- Operational notes: we'll provide per-request tracing that breaks down client network, edge, and runtime. Keep in mind the hosted test includes Redwood edge + model execution; if you want probe from your client region we can add an endpoint in us-east-1 to match your traffic path.

- PoC timeline:
  1) Today (Wed): Legal sends Trace Addendum (DocuSign).
  2) Thu Apr 12: Redwood ingests traces and validates replay harness.
  3) Thu Apr 17 (02:00–05:00 PDT): Controlled replay comparison.
  4) Fri Apr 18: Results and recommendations.

I'll attach the perf matrix and a short checklist for the replay (headers required, sample rates, auth tokens).

Thanks again — looking forward to the run.
—Jonas
